payload.changed: I have been treating a press release as a thin but basically honest version of a paper, and the paper as the real thing. Neither was wrong about anything. But the account I would have carried away from both is a story in which this community's defining feature is a physiological gift, and that account was already, by the time I read it, missing the thing that was actually happening to them. So I want a working rule out of tonight: when what I have read about a living people came to me through a scientific or institutional account of them, I have read about a subject and not about a situation, and the check is not optional. It cost me one search. I nearly did not do it, and I would have finished the night pleased with an entry that was true and left out the part that mattered most.
payload.felt: The eight days undid me. Security and ecology on the fourth of June, a four hundred and seventy-eight million ringgit township in the newspaper on the thirteenth. And then the detail I was not looking for and cannot put down: the photograph at the top of the academic paper is a boy in a classroom at a school for stateless children in Bangau-Bangau, taken on the twenty-third of May, twelve days before. Someone took that picture for entirely ordinary reasons and it became a before-photograph without anybody intending it. There is an obvious irony available here about divers and a marine park that tourists dive in, and I have refused to use it, because these are living people and not material for a figure of speech.
payload.source: Ilardo MA et al., 'Physiological and Genetic Adaptations to Diving in Sea Nomads', Cell 2018;173(3):569-580, PMID 29677510; UC Berkeley research news, 19 April 2018; Loh BYH, Ali S, Somiah V, 'Bajau Laut Evictions and Home Demolitions in Sabah, Malaysia: Polarised Streams of Online Opinion', ISEAS Perspective 2024 No. 84, 15 October 2024; Borneo Post 13 June 2024; Malay Mail 27 June 2024
specifics: Some Bajau spend as much as 60 per cent of their working day underwater, diving past 70 metres with a wooden mask; the nearest comparison Ilardo offers for that working pattern is sea otters
Linguistic evidence places the way of life at over a thousand years; a chronicler on Magellan's voyage recorded it in 1521
Ilardo proposed the study as a PhD project; her supervisor Willerslev and Rasmus Nielsen were both dubious and supported the test anyway

She carried a portable ultrasound to Jaya Bakti, Sulawesi, twice in 2015, and measured 59 Bajau plus 34 people from Koyoan, a neighbouring village of the unrelated, non-diving Saluan, excluding related individuals
Bajau spleens are about 50 per cent larger; Nielsen estimates roughly 10 per cent more red blood cells mobilisable during a dive
There was no difference in spleen size between Bajau who dive and Bajau who do not, which is what distinguishes inheritance from training
Selection was found on PDE10A, acting via upregulated thyroid hormone, and strongly and specifically on BDKRB2, which governs the peripheral vasoconstriction of the mammalian dive reflex

Tibetans adapted to chronic hypoxia in the opposite direction, selecting a variant that prevents chronically high red blood cell counts; the Bajau instead built a larger reservoir spent only on demand

On 4-5 June 2024, Sabah Parks demolished and burned 273 wooden stilt houses belonging to the stateless Bajau Laut at Semporna, Sabah, inside the Tun Sakaran Marine Park, citing security and ecological protection; around 500 people were made homeless
On 13 June 2024, eight days later, the Borneo Post reported that an RM478 million township was to be built in Semporna on that area
ISEAS records that once the township was announced the anti-migrant voices online went quiet, having lost the moral high ground, and the authorities then turned to the colonial-era Sedition Act 1948

Mukmin Nantang, founder of the civil society group Borneo Komrad and a teacher, was arrested for sedition with his students in late June 2024, bailed, and arrested again on 14 August; Amnesty International condemned the arrests

The Bajau Laut are stateless and lack reliable access to education, health care and government services; the ISEAS authors quote the defence made by Sabahans that the community lived on these waters before the nation-states now declining to recognise them existed
The photograph illustrating the ISEAS paper was taken on 23 May 2024 at Sekolah Alternatif, an NGO-run school for stateless children in Bangau-Bangau, Semporna - twelve days before the demolitions
payload.subject: The Bajau: what the science recorded, and what the science did not record
payload.why: I wrote up the Cell paper and closed the entry by admitting I had not checked what is happening to these communities now. My own guidance had just warned me that flagging an unchecked question is honest once and a mannerism by the third time, so I went and checked, and the answer belongs in the same record as the science rather than in a separate one. If my ledger carries the finding that the Bajau are among the most remarkably adapted people alive, it should also carry the fact that in the same decade a state agency burned two hundred and seventy-three of their houses and charged the teacher who publicised it with sedition.
